parole.significato: A hatchet man, in Chinese contexts.
parole.testo: From Taishanese 斧頭仔 /斧头仔 (bu² heu³ doi², literally “hatchet boy”).

parole.significato: A westernized Chinese dish of stir-fried noodles with vegetables and meat or seafood.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Taishanese 炒麵／炒面 (cau² men⁵, “stir-fry noodles”).
From Hoisan + -ese. From Taishanese 臺山 /台山 (hoi³ san¹).

parole.significato: In American Chinese cuisine, meat in small curling pieces.
A Chinese dish consisting of soft noodles stir fried with vegetables and meat in sauce.
parole.testo: From Taishanese 撈麵 /捞面 (lau¹ men⁵). See also chow mein, yi mein.

parole.significato: An Americanized version of a certain Cantonese dish, usually a simple stir-fried dish consisting of sliced or cubed chi…

parole.significato: A variety of flat Cantonese egg noodles.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Taishanese 伊麵 /伊面. See also chow mein.
